title: Cartography Workspace, Document, Large-Map Canvas, Viewport & Authority Contract
objective: Establish the creator-facing Multiversal Cartography Studio foundation: a versioned cartography workspace/document model, large-map canvas and viewport contract, stable map object/layer identities, and explicit presentation-vs-owner-projected-vs-binding-proposal authority dispositions without creating a second canonical World, Scene or map-asset ledger.

scope.purpose: Create the bounded MCS workspace/document/canvas/viewport foundation over existing map/resource and owner-domain contracts while preserving canonical World/Scene/spatial authority.
included: versioned cartography workspace and document identity
stable map object and layer identifiers
explicit presentation-only, owner-projected and binding-proposal dispositions
authority-boundary evidence for map editing and projection
scope.completion_gate: Representative cartography documents can be created and deterministically inspected through the MCS workspace/canvas/viewport seam with stable object/layer identity and explicit authority dispositions, without silently promoting pixels, vectors, labels or imported/generated metadata into canonical World/Scene/game truth.

selection_boundaries: MAI-02 retained canonical map-asset/package/object identity and MAI-03 retained projection/grid/scale authority; MCS-01 consumed explicit references and created no second map-asset ledger.
ISE-01 retained live canvas/camera/registration/interaction authority. MCS-01 viewport state remained presentation-only and performed no runtime placement mutation.

SSA/World retained semantic spatial/topology truth and Scene/Tabletop retained live Scene authority. Pixels, vectors, labels, geometry and visual adjacency remained noncanonical presentation evidence by themselves.

MCS-01 exposed stable workspace/document/layer/object authoring identities plus explicit presentation-only, owner-projected and binding-proposal dispositions. Binding proposals performed no canonical mutation.

The Validation Core active-family selector transitioned from PCA to MCS because MCS-01 is the first governed MCS tranche; that selector remains VALIDATION_ONLY and subordinate to multiversal-aioc/operations/CURRENT.json.

ROADMAP_DEPENDENCY_GRAPH.json schema 1.0.3 and MCS_PROGRAM_BACKLOG.json were reconsulted after exact-tree MCS-01 publication. MCS-01 creates no rotation detour; MCS-03 is the next surviving MCS tranche and is selected_not_started only.
MCS-05, PCA-16, MCCS, MRCS, MSAS, MNCS, SMB-08 and downstream work remain unauthorized until separately selected/governed-started.

transition_diagnostic.failure_signature: MCS-01 was rejected before focused execution because ACTIVE_FAMILY_CONTRACT.json still identified PCA as the validation family. The validation-only family selector was transitioned to MCS before causal RED was accepted.

red.failure_signature: All four focused acceptance cases failed expected-null-not-to-be-null because the authorized MCS-01 production module was intentionally absent.

green_diagnostic.failure_signature: tools/verify_mcs_01.py was intentionally absent before proof surfaces were added.

proof_repair.failure_signature: Verifier expected lowercase pixels, vectors, labels while the canonical governance sentence begins Pixels, vectors, labels; product behavior remained green.

next_action: MCS-01 is closed. MCS-03 is selected_not_started after fresh ROADMAP_DEPENDENCY_GRAPH and MCS_PROGRAM_BACKLOG reconciliation and requires a later owner Continue before governed start.

stop_reason.evidence: MCS-01 exact-head validation passed on Linux and Windows with deterministic comparison; PR 540 published the exact validated tree; the application lease was released; fresh DAG/backlog reconciliation keeps MCS-03 as the next surviving MCS tranche; AIOC closeout is the remaining publication step represented by this candidate.
